subtype: Approach: imagining the party hour by hour in his head [Thinking]
passage: I closed my eyes on the bus and walked through my party like a film. Friends arrive at four, shoes off. We play musical statues at half past four. Cake at five. Everyone leaves at six. Then I saw Ira in the corner of my mind, by herself, holding a glass of juice. She barely knows anyone from my class. I opened my eyes. My plan had nothing for her. So I added a team game where everybody gets a role: one holds the map, one reads clues, one runs. Nobody can hide in a corner. I'm glad I checked it in my head first. Ramya.

qa.q: What time does the cake come in the plan?
What does Ramya notice while imagining the party, and what might Ramya feel about it?
qa.a: Ramya notices the plan has nothing for Ira, who is alone and barely knows anyone, and probably feels concerned and thoughtful about making everyone comfortable.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Ramya use to test the plan, and why?
qa.a: Ramya could tell the plan to a parent or an older cousin and ask what they see missing. Another person may spot a gap that Ramya's own picture leaves out.

qa.q: How does the party look from Ira's point of view?
qa.a: Ira barely knows anyone from Ramya's class, so the party as first planned would look lonely; with a role in the team game, Ira would have a reason to join in.

grounding: A girl imagines the party hour by hour, spots that shy guests have nothing to do and adds a team game with a role for everyone.
